0.0.n: A rustic, informal way to refer to oneself, used here as the character’s distinctive speech.

0.1.n: Links オラ to 映画 to show possession or association.

0.2.n: Japanese nouns do not mark singular or plural; the context indicates multiple films.

0.3.n: Marks the movies as what has reached its 30th anniversary.

0.4.n: 周年 counts completed years since something began.

0.5.n: Combines with 30周年 to describe celebrating the anniversary.

0.6.n: Marks the anniversary celebration as the occasion for the release.

0.7.n: This borrowed word refers here to the Blu-ray editions of the movies.

0.8.n: Marks ブルーレイ as what is being released.

0.9.n: A noun describing a product becoming available to buy.

0.10.n: The plain, casual counterpart of です, used after the noun 発売.

0.11.n: An emphatic sentence ending; writing ぞ as ゾ adds a distinctive visual style.

1.0.n: 懐かしい describes fond feelings about the past; です makes the comment polite.

1.1.n: An extended ね that invites agreement and gives the comment a warm, reflective tone.

2.0.n: Points to the period being shown and directly modifies 頃.

2.1.n: Refers to a period rather than an exact moment.

2.2.n: Links この頃 to オラ, describing the speaker as he was at that time.

2.3.n: The character’s informal self-reference; here it refers to his past self.

2.5.n: Softens the description of how heavy the speaker seems.

2.6.n: 重たい changes to 重たくない for the negative; rising intonation makes this a question inviting agreement.

3.0.n: Gives the length of time the releases will take.

3.1.n: The て-form of かける connects the time spent to the release process.

3.2.n: 発売する becomes 発売して, followed by いく to show the releases continuing into the future.

3.3.n: Adds force and enthusiasm to the announcement, with ゾ representing the character’s distinctive style.

0.lit: My movies, for their 30th-anniversary commemoration, Blu-rays are being released, I tell you!
0.tip: 記念で marks the anniversary celebration as the occasion for the Blu-ray release.

1.tip: The stretched ねぇ invites the listener to share the speaker’s nostalgic feeling.

2.lit: The me of this time, a little heavy, aren't I?
2.tip: A negative adjective with rising intonation, like 重たくない？, often asks for agreement: isn't it heavy?

3.lit: Taking one year, we will keep releasing them, I tell you!
3.tip: ていく shows a process continuing forward, so the releases happen over time rather than all at once.
